title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood of Austin, Texas while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a failure in the perception or decision-making of the autonomous system to recognize and avoid a small animal in its path, even with human oversight active in the vehicle.

The incident occurred in a neighborhood setting where the vehicle was deployed for regular operation, not in a controlled test environment. It would have required either better object detection to identify the duck before impact, or a decision-making system that treats small animals as obstacles to avoid. Whether the human operator could have intervened in time is not established.

In response, Avride acknowledged the accident and stated it is conducting simulation experiments to improve obstacle avoidance. The company disputed an unrelated allegation from residents about a stop sign violation. It is not established whether changes to the system's training or deployment conditions will prevent similar incidents.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, was hit by the self-driving car while it was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. According to a resident's social media post, the vehicle did not slow down or stop after the incident. Local residents have since collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator.

In response to the incident, Avride acknowledged the accident and confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously at the time. The company disputed a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it found no evidence to support this allegation. Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is now conducting controlled simulation experiments to improve the vehicle's ability to avoid similar situations while ensuring such changes do not compromise overall safety performance.
